description:
Child of JMAP-sc1b.17. Add two examples in crate-jmap-chat-client/examples/:
- sse_listen.rs (~80–120 LOC): spins up jmap_chat_server::memory::MemoryBackend behind an in-process push-capable server, subscribes via SSE, prints incoming events.
- ws_loop.rs (~80–120 LOC): same shape but using the WebSocket transport.

Depends on the public MemoryBackend extraction (landed) and on jmap-chat-server's SSE/WS integration.

Acceptance:
- Both examples compile and produce sane output.
- README.md gains links to examples/.
- cargo build --workspace --examples clean.
notes:
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): option (A) — adapted per the bot's analysis since wiremock doesn't support text/event-stream chunked responses and has no WS equivalent.

Rationale: same as .17.4 — server crates are deliberately transport-agnostic (audit confirmed); the bigger 'should workspace own transport?' question is filed as JMAP-l99e (epic). Examples ship now via hand-rolled stubs.

Implementation hint:
  - sse_listen.rs: hand-rolled tokio TcpListener serving one text/event-stream block with synthetic StateChange frames. JmapChatClient (or jmap-base-client::sse::SseConnection) consumes and prints. ~120 LOC.
  - ws_loop.rs: hand-rolled tokio-tungstenite accept loop replying with one Response frame + one StateChange frame. JmapChatClient (or jmap-base-client::ws::WsConnection) consumes and prints. ~120 LOC.
  - tokio-tungstenite added to jmap-chat-client/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies] for ws_loop.rs.
  - README ## Examples section gets a one-liner pointing to each.
  - No new feature flags on the client crate — examples are dev-only.

If JMAP-l99e resolves Yes-own-transport, these examples can be retroactively rewritten to wrap jmap-chat-server::serve_sse() / serve_ws() and drop the hand-rolled listeners.
title: Sub: examples/sse_listen.rs + ws_loop.rs for jmap-chat-client
